subject: Pegasus pilot: clarity on launch credits, commit tiers, and per-token discounts
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@pegasus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot / launch incentive inquiry for Redwood Hosted API

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Pegasus is excited by the latency numbers. We are evaluating a 90-day pilot tied to our Q3 product launch and would like clarity on the incentives you mentioned: free credit buckets, how credits apply to generation vs embeddings, and how commit tiers map to per-token discounts after the pilot.

A few specifics from our side:
- Expected pilot footprint: ~1.2B generation tokens + 200M embedding tokens over 90 days (front-loaded in first 4 weeks).
- Key question: can credits be split between models (generation) and embedding units?
- Do credits expire or roll into committed usage if we convert to a paid tier?

Can you share a sample credit/commit schedule and any constraints (e.g., minimum commit period, ramp requirements)? We want to present a clean ask to finance.

If helpful I can include our procurement lead on follow-ups — looping Carlos.

Best,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Product, Pegasus AI
emma@pegasus.ai

--
Attachment: pegasus_request_form.pdf (form/pdf, 34KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot / launch incentive inquiry for Redwood Hosted API

Hi Emma — great to hear, and thanks for the clear asks. I talked this over with Sales Ops and have sketched a pragmatic path that keeps the pilot simple while protecting your launch economics. High level:

- Pilot length: 90 days (standard).
- Free credits: up to $40k USD in credits usable across generation or embeddings (you choose split). Credits apply to per-token usage; they do not apply to overage per-hour infrastructure surcharges (we don't typically have those on hosted API).
- Credit expiry: credits valid for the 90-day pilot. If you convert to a committed plan within 30 days of pilot end, up to 50% of unconsumed credits can be applied as a one-time rebate against the first invoice of the committed term.
- Commit tiers and discounts (post-pilot):
  * Commit A: $50k/month (12-mo) = 15% per-token discount vs list
  * Commit B: $100k/month (12-mo) = 22% per-token discount vs list
  * Commit C: $250k/month (12-mo) = 30% per-token discount + dedicated support SLA
- Mechanics: commits are monthly USD spend commitments billed monthly; discounts are applied to per-token rates. If you do a 6-mo commit we can provide a smaller premium to the discount (subtract 3 points).

For your numbers (1.4B tokens over 90 days), the pilot credit should cover the first 25-30% of anticipated pilot usage if split evenly. If your embed usage is large we can do a 70/30 split generation/embedding on the credits — tell me your preferred split.

I'll attach the intake form and an initial term sheet for review. Marissa/Ben — can you confirm whether we can allow up to 50% rollover-to-rebate for credits on conversion for this prospect?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos@pegasus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma@pegasus.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot / launch incentive inquiry for Redwood Hosted API

Jordan — quick clarifying questions from finance:

1) If Pegasus signs a 12-month commit after the pilot and we roll 50% of unused credits into a rebate, does that rebate lower our committed billing target for month 1 or is it applied as a credit (i.e., accounting treatment)? We need language we can give to our accounting team.
2) Do credits apply to embeddings at the same unit economics as generation tokens? Our embeddings spend will be mostly for vector search (not expensive models) so we want to make sure we don’t unintentionally undercount.
3) Are there blackout windows or a clause that credits are invalid for promotional months?

Appreciate the clarity.

—Carlos
Carlos Mendes
VP Finance, Pegasus AI
carlos@pegasus.ai

Subject: Internal: Pegasus pilot — credit rollover & accounting note

Jordan/Ben —
Quick internal note so we align with Sales Ops and Finance language. I recommend the following changes before sending to Carlos so accounting has a clean ask:

- Rollover treatment: phrase as a one-time rebate applied to the first invoice (not a reduction to committed target). That makes the accounting treatment clearer (a receivable/credit).
- Credit applicability: explicitly state credits apply equally to generation and embedding token charges (we'll record both as "usage").
- Expiry: credits expire at pilot end; conversion-to-commit must be executed within 30 days to qualify for rebate.
- Doc update: update term_sheet to v2 with the rebate language + sample invoice line items.

Ben — please pull the sample invoice lines and send term_sheet_v2.pdf + pilot_metrics_template.csv back to Jordan so he can loop Pegasus.

Emma/Carlos — thanks for the quick questions. Per internal alignment (see thread):

- Credits: $40k pilot credit, usable across generation and embeddings. Credits expire at pilot end.
- Conversion rebate: up to 50% of unused credits will be issued as a one-time invoice credit applied to the first committed invoice (this is a rebate, not a reduction in committed obligation).
- Embeddings: treated at the same billing category as generation for credit/rebate purposes.
- Commit tiers: committing within 30 days of pilot completion locks in the tier discounts (15/22/30% per our earlier email).

I've attached term_sheet_v2.pdf to this thread (including sample invoice rows and the rebate language) and a pilot metrics template you can use to share expected daily token burn. When you're ready we'll send a DocuSign to Carlos for signature of the committed plan; link included below.
